sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill for a Galveston house?
sections.html:
The Galveston County Tax Office bills and collects for the City of Galveston, for Galveston ISD, for Galveston College and for the county itself, so most island owners get one statement covering several taxing units. Texas has no state property tax, so every dollar on the bill comes from a local unit.

Two offices matter. The Galveston Central Appraisal District sets the value of each parcel as of January 1 and decides who gets an exemption. Its customer service desk takes mail at 9850 Emmett F. Lowry Expressway, Suite A101, Texas City, Texas 77591, and the phone line is (409) 935-1980. The tax office collects the money, accepts mail at 722 21st Street, Galveston, TX 77550, and answers questions about balances at (409) 766-2481.

The county tax office says only the appraisal district can change ownership or mailing address on a parcel. The tax office will pass a correction along as a courtesy, but a seller who moved or a buyer who just closed should file the change with the appraisal district so the next statement reaches the right person.

sections.h2: What is the City of Galveston tax rate for 2026?
sections.html:
The city adopted a 2026 rate of $0.416273 per $100 of property value when City Council approved the FY2027 budget on September 18, 2026. The city's news release describes that figure as the no-new-revenue rate, meaning the rate that raises the same revenue as the prior year from properties taxed in both years.

The same release puts operating funds at about $250.1 million, adds a five-year capital plan of roughly $347.8 million, and notes that the fiscal year runs October 1 to September 30. It also says the city's finances swing with the seasons, which fits an island whose accommodation and food service sales reached $672,706 thousand in 2022 according to the Census Bureau.

The city rate is only one slice. Galveston ISD, the county, Galveston College and any special district such as a navigation or drainage district each adopt their own rate. The Galveston Central Appraisal District lists every unit that taxes a given parcel on its property page, and the Texas.gov property tax database shows proposed and adopted rates during late summer.

sections.h2: When are Galveston property taxes due, and what happens if they are late?
sections.html:
Statements go out in October, and payment is due by January 31 of the following year. Taxes still unpaid on February 1 are delinquent, and the county tax office points out that a postmark after January 31 triggers penalties unless you use one of the payment plans below.

Texas adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest on February 1, with the penalty growing one point a month until it reaches 12 percent on July 1. Interest keeps running at one percent a month with no cap, and a collection attorney's penalty of up to 20 percent can be added to accounts that remain delinquent. A written waiver request goes to the county's Penalty and Interest Committee, and the state allows waivers in limited cases when the tax is paid by the 21st day after the owner learns of the delinquency.

Galveston County Tax Office payment choices
ChoiceRule as the county prints itSource
Single paymentDue by January 31, delinquent February 1County tax office
Split paymentFirst half by November 30, second half by June 30Same page
Quarterly installmentsFour equal payments by January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31 for homesteads of seniors, disabled persons, disabled veterans and their spousesSame page
Payment agreementCall to set one up; it can head off attorney fees added July 1Same page
Advance paymentPay early and write ESCROW in the subject line with the account numberSame page

Online payment by e-check or card carries a fee, the office also takes calls at 1-800-420-1663, and yellow drop boxes sit at each full-time office. Payments by mail should use the 722 21st Street address, because the county warns that the postal service does not always recognize the Moody Avenue address.

sections.h2: How can a Galveston homeowner lower the tax bill?
sections.html:
Start with the homestead exemption, which the appraisal district says is open to anyone who owns and lives in the home. Apply by mail, online or in person, and expect a decision within 90 days of receipt. The general filing deadline is before May 1.

  • School districts must exempt $140,000 of a homestead's value, and owners 65 or older or disabled get an additional $60,000 for school taxes.
  • Any taxing unit may adopt a local percentage exemption of up to 20 percent, with a minimum of $5,000 in value.
  • Owners 65 or older and disabled owners get a school tax ceiling that can follow them to a new Texas homestead, and a surviving spouse aged 55 or older can keep it.
  • Disabled veterans may qualify for exemptions that scale with the VA rating, and a 100 percent rating can mean a total homestead exemption.

The appraised value of a homestead can rise no more than 10 percent a year once the exemption is in place. Owners who think the value is too high can file a protest by May 15, or 30 days after the notice was delivered if that is later. The county tax office also lists a tax deferral affidavit (state form 50-126) among its forms for owners who qualify.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Galveston homes and owners?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated 53,636 residents on July 1, 2025, almost unchanged from the 53,695 counted in the 2020 census, spread over 41.05 square miles of land. Only 46.2 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, which is low for Texas and means a large share of properties are rentals with owners who may live elsewhere.

QuickFacts lists the median value of an owner-occupied home at $326,000 for 2020 to 2024 and median gross rent at $1,298. Median household income is $55,631, and 20.9 percent of residents are 65 or older. That last number matters for property tax, because older homeowners are the group that can qualify for the school tax ceiling and quarterly installments.

The city counts 25,198 households with about 1.98 people each, and the mean commute is 20.2 minutes. Health care and social assistance receipts were $1,608,065 thousand in 2022, a sign of how much of the local economy sits outside the visitor trade.

sections.h2: How do unpaid taxes affect selling a house in Galveston?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax follows the house into a sale. A lien attaches to every Texas property on January 1 to secure that year's tax, and the owner on that date remains liable even if the property later changes hands.

Ask the Galveston County Tax Office for a current statement before listing, and check whether a mortgage servicer already paid the bill through escrow. The county notes that a mortgage code only appears after a lender requests the statement, and it suggests signing up for e-statements in the first year after a payoff or refinance so the bill is not missed.

  • Delinquent taxes, penalties and interest are normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing through the title company.
  • A buyer who closes after January 1 may get the homestead exemption for the rest of that year if the seller did not have it.
  • An owner who cannot pay can ask about a payment agreement after February 1 before choosing to sell.

A house with back taxes, storm repairs or tenants can still be sold as-is to a cash buyer. The key step is getting the payoff figure in writing, so the closing statement shows the tax paid and the lien cleared.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax on a house inside the City of Galveston?
faqs.a: The Galveston County Tax Office collects for the city, Galveston ISD, the county and several other units on one statement. It mails statements in October and takes payment online, by phone, by mail, in drop boxes and in person.

faqs.q: What is the tax rate adopted by the City of Galveston for 2026?
faqs.a: It is $0.416273 per $100 of value, adopted with the FY2027 budget on September 18, 2026. Your total bill also includes the school district, county and any special district rates.

faqs.q: Can I split my Galveston property tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. Pay half by November 30 and the other half by June 30 without penalty and interest. Homesteads of seniors, disabled owners and disabled veterans can instead pay four installments due January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31.

faqs.q: When do I need to file for a homestead exemption in Galveston?
faqs.a: File with the Galveston Central Appraisal District before May 1 for the year you want it. The district acts on an application within 90 days of receiving it and will tell you if you do not qualify.

faqs.q: Does a lien on my Galveston house go away if I sell?
faqs.a: The tax lien does not disappear. The title company pays what is owed from your proceeds at closing, and the owner on January 1 stays liable for that year's tax, so get a payoff statement from the county tax office first.
